name: Central Post Office
summary: Post hall opposite the cathedral: step in for the 1892 and 1936 maps on a short stop from the square. The building is at 2 Công trường Công xã Paris. Alfred Foulhoux and Henri Auguste Vildieu are the named architects, and the materials came from the Eiffel company. Gustave Eiffel is a credit that appears in error.
timeNeeded: A short stop on the cathedral walk. Check on arrival.
fee: Free on the national attractions page. Check on arrival.
getThere: With the cathedral, on the same square.

notice.title: Two architect credits
notice.body: The city tourism page names Alfred Foulhoux and Henri Auguste Vildieu. The national page says Gustave Eiffel is sometimes given the credit in error, and that the design was based on his blueprints.

body: The hall is at 2 Công trường Công xã Paris, Phường Sài Gòn, opposite the cathedral. The national account uses the older label Ben Nghe, District 1. Both names stay. The interior is compared with the Gare d’Orsay. Two painted maps hang at the main door: Saigon and the surroundings in 1892, and Nam Kỳ in 1936. Wooden phone booths and a portrait of Hồ Chí Minh are in the hall, and souvenir stalls line the corridors.

The national attractions page lists admission as free, on a split clock it also uses for other sights. Use the board at the door. The morning cathedral look is the natural pairing. From the Jade Emperor Pagoda the distance is about 2.6 km.
